patch_description: The key observation from the prior programs: all runs plateau at min_area ≈ 0.02 while the best program (score 0.71) used the largest time budget (7s). Random hill climbing with single-point perturbations is extremely inefficient in 26 dimensions. A much stronger approach is a smooth surrogate of the min-area objective optimized by Adam with exact analytical gradients: use a soft-min (negated LogSumExp) over the 286 triangle areas plus a term lifting the k smallest areas (so the bottom of the area distribution rises together rather than one triangle at a time), and a smooth surrogate for the hull area in the denominator. The full gradient of every triangle area w.r.t. all 13 points is computable in closed form and vectorized over all 286 triangles, so each Adam step costs only microseconds — thousands of steps per seed within a 7s budget. We keep a strict min-area evaluation for the true objective (tracking the best feasible configuration seen), add a final bottleneck-targeted polish, and enlarge the time budget to 7s since the 0.71-scoring program shows more time pays off. Seeds are diversified (rings, ellipses, 3-fold symmetric configurations known to be good for Heilbronn).
